correctness.rationale: At t=0 the CG polynomial p0(z)=(1-z/beta)(1-z/gamma) annihilates the two active spectral components. Since the 2x2 Gram matrix of z and z² under positive spectral weights is invertible, the optimum residual polynomial coefficients are analytic in t. The Fréchet derivative of p0(C0) multiplies a cross-cluster F block by p0[beta,gamma]=0, cancelling it exactly. Independent linear adjustments q(beta),q(gamma) remove components along u and v; the first residual derivative is the orthogonal within-cluster perturbation vector scaled by (beta-gamma)/(beta gamma). Squaring in the C0-inverse norm yields the two denominators beta³ gamma² and beta² gamma³, with O(|t|³) error and O(t⁴) when the leading vector vanishes. For symmetric blocks the norm budget for the off-diagonal component z costs 2||z||², giving the exact Frobenius supremum and attaining rank-two block. This proof covers arbitrary finite positive eigenspace dimensions, fixed right hand side with both components nonzero and sufficiently small symmetric perturbations; finite checks are only corroboration.
